title: Why does music give you chills?
description: Why does your favorite song give you goosebumps? Sakumai follows the music from your ears to your brain's reward system and down to the tiny muscles in your skin, and shows the sneaky thing your brain does before the best part.
sources: Salimpoor, Benovoy, Larcher, Dagher & Zatorre (2011), 'Anatomically distinct dopamine release during anticipation and experience of peak emotion to music', Nature Neuroscience 14, 257-262, doi:10.1038/nn.2726, https://www.nature.com/articles/nn.2726 (dopamine is released at the peak of musical pleasure, marked by chills, and already in the anticipation before the peak; chills come with rises in heart rate and other signs of body arousal)

Blood & Zatorre (2001), 'Intensely pleasurable responses to music correlate with activity in brain regions implicated in reward and emotion', PNAS 98(20), 11818-11823, https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.191355898 (music chills activate the brain's reward regions, the same ones that respond to food)

Shwartz et al. (2020), 'Cell types promoting goosebumps form a niche to regulate hair follicle stem cells', Cell 182(3), 578-593, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32679029/ (goosebumps: sympathetic nerves make the tiny arrector pili muscle at each hair follicle contract, pulling the hair upright)

lines.text: Why does your favorite song give you goosebumps?
lines.caps: WHY DOES YOUR | FAVORITE *SONG | GIVE YOU *GOOSEBUMPS?

lines.text: Well, music doesn't just go into your ears,
lines.caps: WELL, *MUSIC | DOESN'T JUST GO | INTO YOUR *EARS

lines.text: it lights up the reward system deep inside your brain,
lines.caps: IT LIGHTS UP | THE *REWARD SYSTEM | DEEP INSIDE | YOUR *BRAIN

lines.text: the same part that loves your favorite food.
lines.caps: THE SAME *PART | THAT LOVES | YOUR FAVORITE *FOOD

lines.text: Then, right at the best part of the song,
it releases a burst of dopamine, a feel-good chemical.
lines.caps: IT RELEASES | A BURST OF | *DOPAMINE | A *FEEL-GOOD CHEMICAL

lines.text: Your heart speeds up a little,
and tiny muscles in your skin pull each hair straight up.
lines.caps: AND TINY *MUSCLES | IN YOUR *SKIN | PULL EACH *HAIR | STRAIGHT *UP

lines.text: before the best part even arrives,
because it can tell what's coming.
So when a song gives you chills,
that's your brain cheering along with you.
